title: The Subscriber That Arrived Late: Durability, the Last Value and How Old Is Too Old

questions.question: A map is published once, then a node starts. Why does the node never see it on an ordinary topic?
options: The map is too large for one message and the pieces are dropped: 0 of 3 late nodes had it
The node subscribes to the wrong incarnation of the publisher: 1 of 3 late nodes had it
Nothing is kept: a subscriber hears what is published after it subscribes, and the map was published once before: 0 of 3 late nodes had it
The queue of a new subscriber starts full, so the first message is lost: 0 of 3 late nodes had it
questions.explanation: An ordinary topic keeps nothing. Whatever was published before a subscriber arrived is gone, and a map published once is never published again.

questions.question: What does a transient local topic do for a subscriber that arrives late?
options: Gives it every message ever published, in order: keep 3 with five published gave 1 2 3 4 5 and then 6
Gives it only the newest remembered message: keep 3 with five published gave 5 and then 6
Gives it the remembered messages after the next live one: keep 3 with five published gave 6 and then 3 4 5
Gives it the remembered messages first, oldest first, then what follows: keep 3 with five published gave 3 4 5 and then 6
questions.explanation: The topic holds its latest few messages. A newcomer gets those first, oldest first, so it catches up before the live stream continues.

questions.question: 1000 messages are published to a topic that keeps 1. What is remembered, and what did an early subscriber hear?
options: 1 remembered, and the early subscriber heard all 1000 once, with no repeats from the late replay
1000 remembered, and the early subscriber heard all 1000 once
1 remembered, and the early subscriber heard 1001, the last one twice
1 remembered, and the early subscriber heard only the last
questions.explanation: The memory is a queue of fixed size, so only the last is kept. A replay is for the subscriber that just arrived and is not repeated to those already there.

questions.question: Why might a subscriber refuse a remembered message?
options: It was sent best effort and may be corrupt
It is too old to be true any more: a goal from a minute and a half ago may be cancelled
It was published by an earlier incarnation of the node
It is larger than the subscriber's queue
questions.explanation: A remembered map is as good as when it was made. A remembered goal may have been replaced or cancelled, so a subscriber can set how old a replay it will take.

questions.question: With remembered messages from 0 s and 98 s, what did a limit of 5 s do at 100 s?
options: Heard 2, since both were remembered, and skipped none
Heard none, since the limit applies to the whole replay
Heard 1 and skipped none: the old one had already been dropped by the bus
Heard 1 and skipped 1, where no limit heard 2
questions.explanation: The message from 98 s was 2 s old and the one from 0 s was 100 s old. The skipped one is counted, so the subscriber knows it was given less than was remembered.

questions.question: What is durability here not?
options: A guarantee that every subscriber gets every message: that is reliability, and it is included
Persistence across a restart: the memory is in the bus and is lost with it, which is a different feature
A memory of more than one message: keep is always 1
A property of the topic: it is set for each subscriber
questions.explanation: The memory lives in the bus. When the bus stops it is gone, and surviving a restart needs storage, which is another feature.
